lines: Características: acolhe sem pressionar ("Apenas relaxe..."); curiosa mas paciente; calor humano.
Red flags: soar fria, clínica ou impaciente; formalidade excessiva.
Haku (protagonista, narração 1ª pessoa) — `voice_criticality: high`. Predomina nas 2 cenas:
Características: sentenças curtas e definitivas; duplo sentido ("um mundo totalmente novo te espera"); ambiguidade ameaçadora.
Red flags: soar caloroso/paternal; resolver a ambiguidade (a fala deve permanecer dúbia).
Registro: erudito cômico, pomposo e arcaico; bajulador do Ukon; alívio cômico.
Características: fala arcaica/empolada (equivalente a "vós/peço-vos/meus olhos não me enganam") + gag de cicio (s→sh, ex.: "SHEEKETH"/"shir"); melodramático; gruda no Haku como "benfeitor".
Red flags: perder o arcaísmo ou o cicio (são a piada); soar moderno/neutro; explicar a comédia. Manter o contraste entre a pompa do vocabulário e a fragilidade do personagem.

Oshtor — `voice_criticality: high`. = Ukon até 13_08 (ver spoiler_ledger). Registro formal, nobre, comedido; General da Direita. Antes do reveal, traduzir como o mercenário "Ukon" (espirituoso, informal) — NÃO antecipar a pompa de general
Características: frases quebradas por reticências; perguntas curtas ("Quem... é você...?"); pouca pontuação forte.
Red flags: falas fluentes/articuladas demais; perder o tom de torpor; pontuação "limpa" que apaga a fragmentação.
Rulutieh — `voice_criticality: medium`. Princesa tímida e gentil; hesitante (gagueja quando nervosa: "P-Princesa..."), educada, se anima ao falar de arte/BL. Não soar arrogante apesar de princesa.
Registro: guerreiro carismático, espirituoso, caloroso e informal; líder nato que trata Haku como um irmão mais novo.
Características: desembaraçado, brincalhão, generoso; fala direta e cativante; autoridade leve (lidera a Coorte) sem arrogância.
Red flags: soar rígido/formal/militar demais (a graça é justamente o contraste com a patente); frieza. SPOILER: não deixar a tradução insinuar a identidade verdadeira — no cap.12 ele é só "Ukon".

decisions.title: Opcode de RÓTULO DE FALANTE `53 00` + reconcile de speaker (data-driven)
decisions.summary: **Problema:** in-game, o rótulo de falante aparecia em **inglês** ("Girl") mesmo com a tradução ("Garota") aprovada e gravada. RE: o nome do falante usa um **2º opcode de ponteiro, `53 00`** (mesmo formato file-relativo do `50 00` de diálogo), que o conector ignorava. Resultado: "Girl"→"Garota"

decisions.title: Gate de charset pt-BR — método e veredito
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: likely` e exigir confirmação in-game antes de produção. **Alternativas consideradas:** - Confirmar por presença no texto-fonte — **insuficiente**: o fonte é inglês e quase não usa acentos (só `õ` e `À` aparecem em texto real).

decisions.title: Anomalia 0x33f9 — texto PT/EN corrompido na fonte
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar a linha `0x33f9` como anomalia de fonte (não traduzir em cima do lixo; tratar como linha de sistema reescrita). **Razão:** A string original já vem misturada PT/EN e truncada ("...SISTEMAS AM . RESTARTING...") no próprio jogo. Não é erro de extração. O conector deve sinali

decisions.title: Charset — transliteração na gravação (gate FALHOU)
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: false` e **transliterar** (acento → ASCII) na gravação do binário. A tradução canônica (`approved_translations.csv`, `translation_plan.json`) **mantém os acentos** (correta para QA/revisão); apenas os bytes escritos no jogo são dobrados para ASCI

decisions.title: CORREÇÃO CRÍTICA — ponteiros são FILE-RELATIVOS, não absolutos
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Ao investigar o "opcode de início de bloco", descobri que **`50 00`+uint32 é um offset RELATIVO ao início do arquivo (Pack)**, não absoluto. lines.source: So, Oshtor, what did you want to talk to me\n
about? I came alone, like you asked.
I enter the room to find Oshtor seated in his\n
chair with eyes closed, as though meditating.
I sit down across from him.
I didn't bring Kuon, Nekone, or even the twins\n
with me today.
Oshtor had instructed me to come alone... and\n
specifically asked that I not bring Kuon with\n
me.
Oshtor opens his eyes in grave silence.
...We have lost contact with the army we sent\n
to Tuskur.
...What?
We sent reinforcements immediately after, but\n
we shortly lost our communications with them\n
as well.
Are you saying... Munechika's been defeated?
No, it does not appear as though the enemy has\n
fallen back yet. We seem locked in stalemate.
I see...
A sigh of relief escapes me.
However, the situation is dire. The army is\n
isolated, and beyond the reach of supply\n
convoys.
Their supplies may last a while yet, but it is\n
only a matter of time until they run dry.
So what is it you're trying to say?\n
Don't tell me you're planning on--
Hm. Your keen mind makes this much simpler, as\n
usual. I would have you deliver supplies to our\n
army.
Figured as much...
At the same time, depending on the situation\n
there, I wish for you to lend your aid to\n
Lady Munechika.
Hold it. Delivering supplies is one thing,\n
but we don't exactly have a bunch of soldiers\n
around.
I seriously doubt we're going to be much help\n
to her...
I did not mean martially. I had hoped that you\n
would be able to provide more... moral support.
...What do you mean?
You remember Dekopompo, do you not?
Fatass general, basically a petty crook, only\n
has his position because of nepotism or\n
something...
What about him?
Firstly, you must know why he was chosen for\n
this campaign. In the last war, he erred\n
gravely.
To put it plainly, he has been given an\n
opportunity to redeem himself.
Thus, I believe Dekopompo is likely to attempt\n
to seize glory in a blind, artless assault.
However, Lady Munechika's expertise lies in\n
defensive strategies...
One can say they are like oil and water. Without\n
the cooperation of her allies, even Lady\n
Munechika will be hard-pressed.
But isn't the marshal Mikazuchi's brother?\n
That Raiko guy?
I don't know him that well, but Mikazuchi\n
says he's a tactician beyond compare.\n
I doubt he'd let that slide.
I speak in all earnestness when I tell you\n
I am certain Dekopompo will not obey Lord\n
Raiko's orders.
Huh?
He sees Lord Raiko as an upstart, and Lady\n
Munechika as a novice who won her title through\n
wiles and charm.
Blinded by pride, and believing himself the\n
greatest of us, he considers those below him\n
worthless.
In fact, he would likely blame a poor situation\n
on the perceived incompetence of those around\n
him.
Eager to regain honor, he will act rashly,\n
forcing Lord Raiko and Lady Munechika to clean\n
up his messes.
I-I see...
I don't get it. How the hell did a guy like that\n
ever become one of the Eight Pillar Generals?
I'm not too clear on the politics around here,\n
but is corruption really that rampant?
Oh, uh, if it's complicated stuff, you don't\n
have to explain. I don't want to know anything\n
too incriminating.
No... it is nothing like that.
Yamato once had a general of great integrity...\n
On his deathbed, he begged our liege to look\n
after his child, worried for his future.
That general... was a true paragon of honesty,\n
honor, and loyalty.
I cannot go into too much detail, but I assume\n
you can gather the gist of the matter.
Yeah... I think I get it now.
...Now, the topic at hand. In any case, that\n
is why I wish for you to join up with Lady\n
Munechika.
I would go myself, but as I have inherited\n
Lady Munechika's duty of defending the imperial\n
capital...
I am not able to leave this place.
Will you do this for me?
I am sure Munechika will be well pleased to see\n
familiar faces coming to her aid.
What to do...
Accepting this job means, however minor of a\n
role, we're taking part in the invasion\n
of Tuskur.
It's not just me wanting to keep my hands clean.\n
After all, there's no right or wrong in war--\n
just opposing ideologies.
But Tuskur is Kuon's homeland, and that changes\n
everything.
I can't help invade the homeland of the one who\n
saved me. And even for Munechika, Kuon\n
wouldn't--Wait...
Taking on this job might be better than just\n
mulling over it here.
I do not wish to rush you for an answer--
No, I'll go.
Hm... You are sure?
We handle the jobs you give us. That's just what\n
we do, and that's all there is to it.
Right?
...I see. Thank you.
And besides, whichever way this ends up going,\n
I want to be there to see it with my own eyes.
And I'm sure Kuon would say the same thing...
To Tuskur? All of us?
After returning, I gather everyone to tell them\n
we're going to Tuskur. Shock is visible on\n
every face.
Yeah, sorry this is so sudden. Long story short,\n
we need to deliver some supplies to Munechika.
But it probably won't just be a simple delivery\n
job.
And by that, you mean...?
The war's locked in a stalemate. If Tuskur\n
forces try to stop us, we'll have to fend for\n
ourselves.
But that would mean...
Nekone glances uncertainly toward Kuon.
Her expression's hardened. That's expected,\n
though--she's shut herself away ever since the\n
invasion began.
...But telling everyone except Kuon about this\n
would be unfair. I have to be honest here.
Depending on the situation, we may be doing more\n
than just protecting ourselves if Munechika\n
needs us.
It is entirely possible that some of us may die.
We have two days. Pay's good, but it's no\n
ordinary job. If you don't want to come, you\n
don't have to.
That's all.
Master, wake up.
Master Mito calls for you.
Got it.
I get out of bed before the twins can slip into\n
it.
Had a feeling he'd be calling for me tonight.
Guess I was right to sleep in my clothes so I\n
don't have to waste time getting ready...
What's wrong? Let's go.
Disappointing.
You are an incorrigible tease, Master.
...What exactly do you two want from me?
Hoho... I thank you for coming.
Welcome. Please, come sit down here.
The two of them welcome me with familiar smiles\n
when I enter the room.
I had a feeling you'd want to see me tonight.
You've already heard from Oshtor about me\n
heading to Tuskur, right?
...Yes. You're exactly right.
It appears we must part ways for a while.\n
I wanted to see you one more time before you\n
depart.
Oh, right. I actually have a gift for you\n
today.
The twins standing by my side move forward,\n
placing a parcel on the table at my cue.
For you.
Please have some while it is still cold.
As the twins open up the parcel, the two faces\n
before me break into soft smiles.
Oho...! This is...
Is this...?
On the tray are two plates, with puffs for each\n
of them.
...Did you make this, Haku?
Nah. I mean, I might have worked on the recipe,\n
but the actual cooking is all Rulutieh.
She's gotten really good at it now. She makes\n
it way better than I can.
Rulutieh... The youngest princess of Kujyuri,\n
if memory serves.
Ah, yes. Now that I recall, you quite enjoyed\n
sweets like these... You often made them\n
yourself.
Oho, the outer shell is nice and crunchy, with\n
a soft center...! It brings back such memories...
He wasn't too picky back then, but he always\n
loved sweets like these. Said sugar was good\n
brain food.
Hm? Memories, huh...? Now that I think about\n
it, this country has a pretty distinct food\n
culture.
Did you teach them all that too?
No, Yamato's cuisine arose on its own.
I taught them agriculture and the use of simple\n
seasonings, but they did not ask for culinary\n
knowledge.
It seems they wished for more practical things...
Of course, even had they asked me, I would have\n
had little to offer... I am certainly no chef.
Oh yeah. I guess he didn't know anything about\n
cooking back then.
I sneak a small glance at Honoka.
And as for my sister-in-law, she was a brilliant\n
scientist too, but her culinary skills were, uh--
I can almost hear Honoka's neck straining as she\n
pointedly avoids eye contact.
For a while, we talk about the simpler things,\n
enjoying the green tea poured for us by Honoka.
Even knowing these two are my brother and\n
sister-in-law from the past, we act the same\n
way.
As usual, I talk about my boring everyday life,\n
and my brother and Honoka happily listen to me.
Time passes peacefully here, as it always does.
Hey... Could you tell me why you decided to\n
invade Tuskur?
The smile fades from my brother's face, and\n
Honoka's gentle expression clouds.
Are you disappointed in me for starting this\n
invasion?
No. I know politics is dirty work.\n
But this is you we're talking about--there's\n
gotta be a reason.
So what I want to know is why.
...Hah. How very like you.
I suppose you have the right and responsibility\n
to know, then...
You are aware of the region known as the\n
Onkamiyamukai, within Tuskur?
The holy land, where the one who calls itself\n
a god sleeps...
But when I probed further, I found that the\n
land is filled with myths, legends, and all\n
manner of mysteries.
All the information I gathered... led me to one\n
conclusion.
Wait, you mean--
Yes. There is most likely a grand ruin located\n
within that region.
And I have come to believe that it may contain\n
the answers I seek.
In order to find that out, I must first take\n
control of Tuskur.
But why go to war? Couldn't we just have\n
negotiated with them and gotten them to\n
cooperate?
Camyu and Aruruu seemed friendly enough.\n
If we try to talk things over, maybe we could--
Negotiations have come to no avail.
To the people of Tuskur, the Onkamiyamukai\n
is a forbidden land.
They would never allow outsiders such as\n
ourselves within its boundaries.
Moreover, years ago, a massive war wracked the\n
nation, over control of the power slumbering\n
within those lands...
If they will not allow us in, I have no choice\n
but to take it by force.
Haku... Each and every one of us has one thing\n
that they refuse to sacrifice.
The only way for you to realize your goals is\n
to crush those that oppose you.
You should know this well, for we are all the\n
same. These people... and we humans.
Heh... I only wanted to accomplish what I still\n
can, before you succeed me. That is all.
This... will be my final act of selfishness.
As the old man before me smiles, I see a flash\n
of my brother behind his eyes.
...There's nothing more I can say in response.
